title: Roy Palmer and Chicago's South Side
summary: Russell reports on Roy Palmer, and they sort out where the Royal Garden and other Chicago places stood.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I wish I'd brought some pictures of Roy Palmer, but I'll send you a picture to show you the way Roy looks. He looks wonderful. He looks as good and young as ever. He really does.
Yeah, he looks almost like he does in that picture, doesn't he?

Yeah, he's hardly changed. His hair isn't gray. I'm not, I'm trying to, I don't have any hair at all. I don't have any. I don't have any. But Roy looks, his hair is still dark and he doesn't play trombone anymore, but he's still interested in it.
He had a loan in the Alva Wood six, seven years back.
Well, he gave that up on his own Wells Street, about 51, can't remember the number.
I can easily get that because I got a nephew there. He's an extra specialist at Chicago. I got two or three there, a barber.

Yeah, well, I'll send you that number anyway. All right, I appreciate that. It's down near 51st Street in Wells, across from the little school. And his wife used to play trombone too. She was very wealthy. I don't know if you knew her, but I don't think she came from here.

No, I don't remember. He had no wife up there. He had a bar woman. That sometimes works out for the best. Well, we read something, Ron, if you remember one? Oh yeah, we had the time. Green Miner. Ha ha ha ha. 239. How you call that street? Roads, eh? Yeah. Where Jesus is there. Roads have one.
That's where the Royal Garden is right on that road.
No, Royal Garden was that was in College Grove.
Oh, I thought the roads ran in there too, didn't it?

the 35th Street up there. 35th Street. It's all torn down. Everything is down there. Dreamland and 35th Street may be there. Porter's Drugswood, that's down too. Upstairs, all that's down. One of the E-Lights is there. One of them is there at 35th and the State.
He liked number two. Number two. Keep enjoying that.
